paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.
model_annotation: This plot compares the performance of two methods, ST-ES and Random, in terms of their minimum FDE20 (Final Displacement Error at top 20 predictions) values as the number of in-context examples varies. The x-axis represents the "Number of Examples" with a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 8, and is labeled at intervals of 2. The y-axis represents "minFDE20" with a linear scale, ranging from 17 to 24, and is labeled at intervals of 1. The blue line representing ST-ES starts at approximately 21.5 when the number of examples is 0 and decreases to around 17.2 at 6 examples, before slightly increasing to about 17.3 at 8 examples, with a solid line and circular markers. The orange line representing Random starts at approximately 24 when the number of examples is 0 and decreases to around 21.7 at 8 examples, with a solid line and circular markers, remaining above the ST-ES line throughout the range.
